key_insight: Twist angle in multilayer H-MoS2 can actively tune and enhance shift-current photocurrents by breaking symmetry and modifying electronic wavefunctions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests moiré engineering as a design knob for next-generation photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices that harvest light via the bulk photovoltaic effect rather than p-n junctions.
method: Built a Slater-Koster tight-binding model for large moiré supercells, parametrized from first-principles calculations.
Compared electronic structures and shift-current spectra against DFT and Wannier-interpolated results.
Analyzed mono-, bi-, and trilayer H-MoS2 plus twisted bilayer and trilayer configurations.
evidence_signal: The model was validated by agreement with first-principles electronic band edges and by reproducing the main spectral features of the shift-current conductivity.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on how well the tight-binding parametrization transfers to other twist angles, layer counts, or material variants beyond the calibrated systems.
paper_title: Twistronic control of shift current in multilayer moiré system
